chapter: Return to Chicago: the Blue Note and Rupneck's
title: The Blue Note plan to replace the band with stars
summary: Hodes learns Williamson plans to swap in Zutty, Wild Bill and Brunis and build the Dixielanders as a package. DeMichael says this booking practice later hurt the club.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: But this was the first Blue Note.

This was on -- I don't know if it was the first or the second. It was on Madison Street, and I think it was down in the basement. That was it. And they played Louis Armstrong in that place. Now, the plan starts to unfold here, I didn't know when I got when I hired these guys. And the plan is that we're going to replace Freddie Moore with Zutty Singleton. We're going to replace Lee Collins with Wild Bill Davis. We're going to replace Floyd O'Brien with George Brunis. And we're going to get Bechet to get on and get offstage, as a star.
Whose plan was this, Frank Holsteins?
Armstrong has got his band, the small band on the road, and it's a big deal. Let's build the Dixielanders, and if they want Louis, they got to take the Dixielanders next. That's the clout.
Yeah. And the next time around, you don't have to worry, we'll kill them. They'll take us, anyway. That's the -- now I got to tell Freddie Moore he's through.
That's what eventually killed the Blue Note, according to Frank Holstein. If you wanted Duke, you had to take Joe Blow.
